conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, aiming for steady, low-drawdown performance.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing new high-quality setups, aiming for a blend of stability and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. This approach carries substantially higher risk, including potential for larger drawdowns and daily decay in leveraged products, requiring strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Increase QQQI to 30% and QQQ to 20% to prioritize income and broad index.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to exit high-beta single names.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It rotates into income and broad index ETFs while cutting high-beta single names and all leverage. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
